## TL;DR

I ran a scripted headless-WebKit QA pass over the app's three transient surfaces
together — the shared toast stack (`ToastPanel`), page-level banners, and modal
dialogs — at 375, 768 and 1280 px, driving everything through preview-board
fixtures plus deliberate route interception. It found one real, user-visible bug
class: floating surfaces that share the toast stack's top-right corner covered
the stack and left its dismiss buttons dead. The recovery banner (z-index 1000,
top-centered, near-full-width on phones) hid all five toasts with every close
button unreachable; the notice-bell popover was overlapped by toasts at every
width. Both are fixed with one mechanism: the covering surface publishes its
bottom edge as a CSS custom property and the toast panel drops below it, clearing
the var when the surface goes away. On a resumed session I merged a much newer
main into the branch, re-verified the scripted pass myself, and found its
dialog/drawer/banner checks racing fixture re-application and UI entrance
animations — three harness-timing bugs fixed so the 63 scripted checks pass
cleanly on three consecutive runs, with component-level regression tests, a new
`toast:stack` preview fixture, and the QA doc at
`docs/qa/2026-11-toasts-banners-dialogs-qa.md`.

## Work and rationale

The criteria asked for headless-Playwright-only verification against fixtures,
several surfaces triggered at once, fixes backed by tests, and a committed QA
doc.

**Verification harness (`docs/qa/measure-toasts-banners-dialogs.mjs`).** The app
under test is the freshly built `dist/ui`, served from a throwaway empty fixture
root through the shared UI harness `repoos check`'s smoke gate uses — never the
live board, always headless WebKit; `REPOOS_PREVIEW_CHILD=1` turns `?shotState=`
fixtures on. The script probes real geometry, real hit-testing
(`elementFromPoint` at each dismiss control's center — the honest answer to "is
this button dead?"), and real dismissal (actual clicks and keyboard Enter), and
exits non-zero on any failure.

**A stacked-toasts fixture (`toast:stack`).** Nothing could produce several
toasts at once, so I registered the fixture and applied it in the UI's fixture
switch: five pinned toasts (error, success, info, one multi-line) written
directly to the store, bypassing `pushToast` so no 6 s auto-expiry timers are
armed — captures and probes always see the same stack. A fake-timer test proves
the stack survives timer advance.

**Six scenarios per width.** Toast stack layout/overlap/dismiss; the board
load-error banner on both surfaces; the `release:updateAvailable` dialog (fit,
Escape, Close ×); the task drawer opened over the stack; the recovery banner
raised over it; and the notice-bell popover opened over it.

## Approaches tried

One scenario taught the most. My first board-banner test used the existing
`work:failedLoad` fixture and expected Retry to clear the banner. It never did,
though the fetch visibly returned 200 with valid JSON. Chasing that through the
live app's Pinia store uncovered a design fact: `refresh()` re-applies the
capture fixture at the end of every successful reload (#0782/#0834) so a
fixture-seeded board survives SSE-driven refreshes. A fixture-pinned error state
therefore *cannot* model "retry works" — the pin is the point. I switched that
scenario to a real failure (route-aborting `/api/board` before page load, then
lifting it before clicking Retry), testing the actual dismissal path on both
banner surfaces. That same fact came back as the central bug of the resumed
session.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Worktree files were checked out read-only (0444)**; a formatter pass failed
  with EACCES until I `chmod u+w`'d the touched paths, and the reaped harness
  `TMPDIR` broke `mkdtemp` until recreated.
- **Timing flakiness in the popover scenario.** Measuring the popover once on
  open left a stale published drop when async notice content grew it. I made the
  component honest — a `ResizeObserver` republishes the drop on size changes —
  and kept a settle wait in the script.
- **A crashed prior turn left a concurrent writer**, and the first scoped check
  failed its worktree-drift gate. I verified no runner was live, confirmed the
  tree went quiet, reviewed every foreign edit, and re-ran the gate on the
  stable tree.
- **Remote validation flaked three times on timing, not code** — a different
  wall-clock-sensitive test each attempt, each passing locally in isolation;
  the untouched fourth attempt passed, confirming load, not code.
- **The branch had fallen 157 commits behind main.** My first re-run of the
  scripted pass failed at the dialog scenario; staleness was a suspect, but the
  failure reproduced identically after a conflict-free merge of main and a
  rebuild — a real timing bug, not drift.
- **The dialog Escape check raced fixture re-application.** Instrumented probes
  (dismissable-layer enumeration, then rAF presence sampling) caught it
  red-handed: the dialog closed at 38 ms and *reopened* at 58 ms, because the
  post-refresh fixture re-run sets the dialog's `open` back to true (#0782). A
  press inside that window gets undone — a ~20 ms blink the polling wait can
  miss — and separate rounds caught presses being lost outright in the page's
  first moments. Fix in the harness, not the app: settle 1.5 s before every
  keyboard dismissal, one guarded retry against lost key delivery, and pass
  `undefined` for `waitForFunction`'s `arg` — the script had been passing
  `{ timeout }` as the arg parameter, so every wait silently used the 30 s
  default.
- **The drawer close button and recovery banner had races too.** Frame-by-frame
  rect sampling showed the drawer slides in from off-viewport, so a probe during
  the animation found the close button's centre outside the viewport —
  `elementFromPoint` null, the exact signature of a dead control. The banner
  scenario's single focus nudge could join the still-in-flight startup health
  check and be consumed with no fresh probe seeing the aborted API. Both now
  wait for a real precondition — the button's centre inside the viewport; the
  banner actually up (bounded nudge loop) — rather than a bare sleep.

## Key learnings

- **Hit-testing beats geometry.** Two surfaces can overlap without either being
  "dead" (a modal legitimately paints over a toast), and non-overlapping-looking
  rects can still hide a control. But `elementFromPoint` returning null doesn't
  prove covering either — mid-animation the centre can sit outside the viewport.
  Instrument (rect + hit-test sampled per frame, keydown delivery logged) before
  changing component code.
- **Shared-corner floating surfaces need a coordination channel.** Each surface
  now publishes `--toast-panel-drop-*` and the panel takes `max()`; the vars are
  independent so writers compose, and every close path must clear its own var —
  the component tests pin exactly that, because a missed close path strands the
  stack 200 px too low.
- **Fixtures pin state; behavioural QA must cause its own failures — and wait
  for the pin to settle.** Anything asserting recovery must produce the failure
  via interception, then wait past the re-application window, or the pin undoes
  it a frame later.
- **A "passing" script can still be wrong.** The `waitForFunction` arg bug made
  every intended 5 s timeout a silent 30 s; assertions about timing deserve a
  test of the test.

All acceptance criteria are met: headless-only QA, several surfaces triggered
together via `toast:stack` plus registered fixtures and real clicks, both
dead-dismiss findings fixed with component tests, the QA doc written, and the
scoped check green end to end on the post-merge tree — including remote
validation on thinkpad — with the scripted 63-check pass green on three
consecutive runs, the last on the final formatted tree.
